relatedSnapshot.title: Cold Email: follow-up step delay applied one step off — final follow-up sends ~1 day early instead of configured delay
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:
Customer: Name 1 (<email>). Workspace: Company Four (org <uuid>). Campaign: "AMM Conference July 26-29, 2026" (id <uuid>), provider Company One, provider_campaign_id <uuid>.

Symptom: the second follow-up (Step 3, subject "Great being part of AMM Name 4" — a post-conference message) was configured to send 9 days after the prior step but went out ~1 day after Step 2, i.e. ~8 days early and before the conference it references. Customer paused the campaign because the premature follow-up made the outreach look automated ahead of a conference where he is a featured speaker.

Data:

* Stored provider sequence (outreach_campaign.metadata.providerData.sequences[0].steps): step[0].delay=2, step[1].delay=1, step[2].delay=9. step[2] is the post-conference email the customer set to 9 days.
* Provider webhook events (outreach_webhook_event) for representative leads: step 1 sent 2026-07-16, step 2 sent 2026-07-22, step 3 sent 2026-07-23. The step2->step3 gap = 1 day, which matches step[1].delay=1, NOT the step[2].delay=9 the customer configured for that follow-up.

Root-cause hypothesis (off-by-one between editor and provider delay semantics):

* Provider treats a step's delay as the wait AFTER that step (before the next). See apps/web/lib/outreach/emailbison/client.ts: read maps `delay: normalizeDelay(group.main.wait_in_days)`, write maps `wait_in_days: step.delay`.
* The sequence editor (apps/web/components/campaigns/detail/tabs/sequences/sequence-breakdown-editor.tsx) renders the delay control BETWEEN step cards and writes it to `stepIndex = group.stepNumber + 1` (the NEXT step), with aria-label "Delay in days before sending next message".
* Net effect: every configured delay is applied one step off, and the LAST step's delay is effectively ignored. The customer's 9-day value landed on the final step (which governs nothing), while the actual gap before the final follow-up was taken from the previous step's delay (1 day) -> follow-up fired ~1 day after Step 2.
* Help Center (apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/campaigns/managing-campaigns/sequences.mdx) documents the intended behavior as "Step 2, sent 2 days after Step 1" (delay = wait before this step), which the observed behavior contradicts.
* The campaign was paused 07-17..07-22 and resumed 07-22 (when the 07-16 cohort's follow-ups fired). Pause/resume explains the timing of the batch but does NOT explain a configured 9-day inter-step gap collapsing to 1 day — that is the delay-mapping defect.

Sources: Prod DB (read-only), codebase. Sentry: no related runtime errors (this is a silent mapping bug, not a thrown exception). Axiom: unavailable (token expired). No existing Name 2 issue matches this exact symptom (closest thematically: ENG-8367, done, different symptom).

Secondary item (NOT a bug): customer also asked why only ~95 of 218 leads were sent. DB shows 216 active leads: 195 contacted, 10 not_yet_contacted, 4 interested, 3 out_of_office, 2 reply_received, 1 not_interested, 1 bounced; sends were spread across days (07-16: 139, 07-22: 98 new + 50 follow-ups, 07-23: 10). This is expected gradual sending (daily volume caps + sending window + multiple uploads/deletions) and is covered by existing Help Center docs. No docs gap.

POTENTIAL FIX:
Align the delay write-index in sequence-breakdown-editor.tsx with the provider's per-step delay semantics so a between-step delay maps to the gap the user sees, and ensure the final step's configured delay is honored (or consistently surfaced). Verify the wait_in_days<->delay round-trip in emailbison/client.ts and add a regression test for step-delay ordering.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

1. Name 3 provider's wait_in_days semantics and the exact editor->provider index mapping.
2. Correct the mapping and add a step-delay round-trip regression test.
3. Optionally recompute/repair pending follow-ups for affected campaigns so already-scheduled follow-ups honor configured delays.

INTERCOM: <url:app.intercom.com>
SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
DEVIN SESSION: <url>

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: cold email follow-up sent minutes after the first email instead of the configured 3-day delay (Meat processors MN campaigns)
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Intercom source**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Conversation context**: 2026-10-01 the customer (workspace "Name 6's Workspace") first asked for a team member, then reported that either his two newest campaigns are not working or the stats he sees are wrong. Asked for workspace and campaign names he named the workspace under his name and the campaigns "Meat processors MN – beef/hog" and "Meat processors MN – A leads": the A leads campaign "says it sent out the second email in the sequence right after sending the first email. There should have been a 3 day delay between emails", and the beef/hog campaign "says it has some issue that needs attention". On 2026-10-03 he asked again for a reply, saying he cannot start another email campaign until he knows whether this is fixed or not a problem. Conversation open, unassigned.

**Claim**: In "Name 6's Workspace", cold email campaigns "Meat processors MN – A leads" (launched 2026-09-30) and "Meat processors MN – beef/hog" (launched 2026-10-01) sent sequence step 2 to each lead 14 minutes to \~2 hours after step 1 instead of the configured 3-day delay, because the app writes each step's "days to wait before this step" value into the Company One step field whose documented meaning is the wait before the next email, so every wait is applied one step late and the final step's wait is ignored.

**Evidence (2026-10-05, read-only)**

* Company One provider email records, campaign "Meat processors MN – A leads" (provider campaign <uuid>): step 1 subject "phones during deer season" sent in batches 16:02:55-18:04:49 UTC 2026-09-30; step 2 subject "Re: phones during deer season" sent 18:19:24-20:03:26 the same day, on the same thread as each lead's step 1 (e.g. one lead 18:04:49 then 18:19:24, another 16:02:55 then 18:19:24). 23 of 26 leads got step 2 (2 bounced, 1 replied, stop_on_reply true).
* Same pattern on "Meat processors MN – beef/hog" (provider campaign <uuid>): step 1 15:05:57-15:34:11, step 2 15:44:11-16:20:07 on 2026-10-01. 8 of 8 leads got both steps (16 delivered).
* Company One's live campaign config still carries the intended delay: step 1 delay 0, step 2 delay 3 with delay_unit "days".
* The app's own contract says the value is the wait before the step: the public API documents attach-sequence delayInDays as "Days to wait before sending this step. First step is typically 0." (apps/api/src/schemas/campaigns.ts), and the sequence editor labels the control "Delay in days before sending next message". Company One's API documents sequences\[\].steps\[\].delay as "the delay value before sending the NEXT email", and Company One's help centre states the delay configured under Step 1 determines when Step 2 is sent.
* Code: applyExactCampaignSequence maps delayInDays straight to the provider's per-step delay (apps/web/lib/outreach/apply-exact-campaign-sequence.ts, commit c5e3314fd5f9295021cd1f4d6bc8032c4f82473e), and writeCampaignSequenceToProvider PATCHes those steps to the provider unchanged.
* Blast radius (counted 2026-10-05): 101 campaigns across 51 organizations that have sent have a first-step delay of 0, which under this mapping sends the first follow-up immediately after the first email; 11,390 sending campaigns across 2,483 organizations have a multi-step sequence and therefore a one-step-off wait.
* Same workspace, same defect, different campaign: "Name 7 | FinServ | LinkedIn Name 8 | R1" (delays 0,3,3,7) sent 40 emails for 20 leads on its first day, then one step per 3 days, matching the shift.

**Secondary finding (already tracked elsewhere)**: "Meat processors MN – beef/hog" carries pause_reason "Provider reported the campaign completed, but no emails were sent. Re-verify the leads and restart the campaign." although 16 emails were delivered, because its 8 campaign-lead rows still read not_yet_contacted with no status event and no provider_lead_id. Same class as ENG-14098 (lead status writeback missing); it is what makes the app warn about a campaign that did send.

**Impact**: follow-up spacing customers configure is not honoured (follow-ups arrive early; on step-1-delay-0 campaigns, minutes after the first email), and campaigns complete and stop within hours of launch, which also blocks the customer from launching further campaigns.

Now he feels burned because he lost time with no real progress, and also wasted money buying domains, accounts, and subscriptions on Company One and ReachOutly that he can’t use with us.

He vented quite a lot on a call with me just now, and also earlier during office hours. This has definitely escalated. He’s clearly upset and is blaming us for the wasted time and money.

To calm things down and avoid further escalation, I walked him through how we’ll set things up properly moving forward, and I offered some credits to make up for the situation. I told him we would cover inboxes and domains, plus give him some extra time on the platform since he now has to go through the warm-up process again.

What I agreed on the call:

1. 12 DFY inboxes covered for 3 months
2. Custom domains covered for 1 year
3. 1 month of Acquisity for free


If possible, I’d like to extend the Acquisity credits to 2 months instead of 1, just to go a bit above what was promised and help smooth things over further. If that’s not possible, no worries, but at least the 1 month should definitely be added.

Let me know if we can get these credits applied asap.

relatedSnapshot.title: One-off recovery: backfill + AI SDR replay for the webhook-outage cohort (99 + 207)
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Reopened 2026-06-23 per James (Slack P0 thread) — this is the live one-off recovery run for the webhook-outage cohort.** Previous cancellation reversed so the resync → backfill → AI-SDR-replay is tracked on record (not just in-flight Slack work).

## Problem

During the silent webhook outages, prospect replies arrived while webhooks were down. We've resynced + backfilled most affected workspaces but have NOT re-run AI SDR on those imported replies — importing does not trigger AI SDR (verified in code) — so prospects sit un-answered. Several clients have had this for a couple of weeks and think their campaigns aren't working.

Cohorts: 99 (May-20) resynced+backfilled, not replayed; 207 active-campaign silent dropouts (158 resynced+backfilled, ~49 pending resync, none replayed); plus the two named system-provisioned workspaces `<workspace-slug>` and `<workspace-slug>` (whose admin "resync" never actually re-registered — confirmed via Inngest: no resync run fired).

## Plan (one-off scripts; reuse existing primitives; no new app code)

Strictly ordered, with wait points (ordering is load-bearing):

0. **Detect** — read-only script: active Company One provider + ≥1 active campaign + 0 `outreach_webhook_event` in last N days → org-id list. Confirm count ≈ cohort and that the two named workspaces appear.
1. **Re-register** — fire `OUTREACH_EVENTS.RESYNC_WEBHOOKS` per org (batched; `processResyncWebhook` caps concurrency at 5; uses the shipped create-then-swap from PR #4945). Wait for completion.
2. **Backfill (windowed)** — `OUTREACH_EVENTS.EMAIL_THREADS_BULK_IMPORT` `{ organizationIds, userId: <superadmin>, classifyInterest: true }`. Wait for completion.
3. **Replay** — select positive / last-from-prospect / non-human-owned / non-terminal threads → `admin.sdrReplay.replayThreads` in ≤300-id batches (re-verifies prospect-sent-last before firing).

Depends on PR #4945 (the safe-resync prerequisite). Every driver script ships with a `--dry-run`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All affected orgs (99 + 207 + the 2 named) re-registered and confirmed delivering.
- [ ] Missed messages backfilled (windowed to the silent period; no full-history walk).
- [ ] AI SDR replayed on unanswered prospect threads; no double-replies (idempotency/guards respected).
- [ ] Never replays human-owned (`controlLevel` in human_takeover/dnc/paused/escalated) or terminal-lifecycle (booked/completed/declined) threads.
- [ ] Per-phase structured summary (orgs resynced, threads imported, replays fired/skipped/failed).

Name 29 this flow (auto on every future reconnect) → ENG-10710. Detection / zombie webhooks → ENG-10661 + ENG-10711.
